title: Jude and the Compass
premise: Sebastian Coldharbour, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate, takes a job from his old rival Mara Quill: escort a survey crew across the Kestrel Range before the snows close the passes. The route runs through Coldharbour Hollow, the valley Sebastian swore never to re-enter after a storm took his brother and ended his engagement to Jude Ashcombe, who still lives there. When the syndicate's collectors follow them into the range, Sebastian must choose between paying with the survey's stolen data or losing his crew. In the end he surrenders the data, confesses everything to Jude, and survives the crossing broke but unburdened — learning that stopping was never what cost him; running was.
about_author: Rosalind Underhill is a former mountain guide who turned to writing adventure fiction after a decade of leading expeditions across three continents. She lives in a converted fire lookout tower, where she writes about people caught between the weather and their own pasts.

chapters.title: The Debt of Clear Skies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A failed chase leaves his crew unpaid and the Vane Syndicate circling, so when rival Mara Quill offers a fortune for a pre-winter crossing of the Kestrel Range, he signs without reading the route — until he sees it ends at Coldharbour Hollow. The beat is dread disguised as relief: money in hand, a door he swore shut swinging open.

chapters.title: What the Valley Remembers
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The crew arrives at the hollow, where Jude has built a careful life around her grief and her fury at Sebastian's return. Forced to guide them through the pass she knows best, she trades barbs that keep cracking into honesty. The beat is old love resurfacing against her will, duty to her town pulling against the pull of him.

chapters.title: Whiteout Terms
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The syndicate's collectors ambush the party mid-range as an early blizzard seals the passes; they demand the survey's data as payment, or the crew freezes. Mara reveals she planned the theft all along, and Jude learns Sebastian sold years of her valley's maps to fund his escape. The beat is betrayal compounding betrayal as survival strips everyone to their debts.

chapters.title: The Price of Stopping
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converge at the pass. Sebastian burns the data rather than let the syndicate strip-mine the hollow, choosing Jude and the crew over solvency, and they shelter together through the storm that once took his brother. Emerging to cleared skies, he stays in the hollow — broke, forgiven, finally still. The beat is love chosen over flight, survival paid in full.
